chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Umar al-Zayyat, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) - regarding the making up of the night prayer after dawn until the sunrise. He said, 'Yes, and after Asr until nightfall, and it is from the hidden secret of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.سِرِّ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The secret of the Family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: When can the missed night prayer be made up according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Hadi (AS), the ruling for making up the night prayer (Salat al-Layl) is extended beyond the immediate post-dawn window to include the period from after Asr until nightfall, a flexibility often regarded as a 'hidden secret' (Sir) of the Ahl al-Bayt due to its nuanced jurisprudential implications. This highlights the unique scholarly tradition of the Imams, where specific timings for voluntary acts carry deeper spiritual or legal significance known primarily to the learned. The designation as a 'secret' underscores the depth of knowledge preserved within the Imamate regarding the subtleties of worship.
